name: Oak Steakhouse
desc: Charleston-born steakhouse at Avalon known for dry-aged beef, Wagyu and ribeyes, backed by an extensive wine list. One of Alpharetta's go-to special occasion rooms.
tips: Book ahead for weekend evenings
The bar is a good walk-in option for a quicker steak night

name: South City Kitchen Avalon
desc: Upscale Southern cooking at Avalon, known for fried chicken, biscuits, shrimp and grits and one of the area's most popular brunches.
hours: Breakfast Mon-Fri 7-10am; Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-2pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 8am-2pm; Dinner Mon-Thu 5-9pm, Fri-Sat 5-10pm

name: Rumi's Kitchen
desc: Persian dining at Avalon known for juicy kabobs, fragrant rice and hummus. A metro Atlanta favorite that made Avalon a food destination.

name: Colletta
desc: Northern Italian at Avalon with wood-fired pizza and house-made pasta in a lively dining room.

name: Antico Pizza
desc: The Avalon outpost of Atlanta's famed Neapolitan pizzeria, with blistered wood-fired pies, gelato and cappuccino.
hours: Mon-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm; Sun 11am-8pm (closes when dough runs out)

name: Superica
desc: Ford Fry's Tex-Mex cantina at Avalon, known for chorizo queso fundido, sizzling fajitas and a popular Sunday brunch.

name: The Cape Restaurant & Beach Bar
desc: Cape Town-inspired coastal restaurant at Avalon with a sunset rooftop and a crab dip locals rave about.

name: MF Bar
desc: Sushi rolls, nigiri and a deep sake list served around a big U-shaped bar at Avalon.

name: CRU Food and Wine Bar
desc: Wine bar at Avalon with build-your-own cheese flights, shareable plates and a people-watching patio.

name: Barleygarden Kitchen & Craft Bar
desc: Gastropub at Avalon with 60+ craft beers on tap, burgers and sandwiches and a dog-friendly patio.

name: Branch & Barrel
desc: Craft cocktails and elevated American fare at Avalon, known for the corn fried lobster sandwich and crispy Brussels sprouts.

name: Ted's Montana Grill
desc: Bison specialist at Avalon known for its 50/50 beef-bison burger and classic American comfort plates.

name: Cafe Intermezzo
desc: Paris-style bistro and coffeehouse at Avalon with towering dessert cases, crepes, tarts and late-night espresso.

name: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams
desc: Beloved scoop shop at Avalon with inventive flavors and fresh waffle cones.

name: Smokejack Southern Grill & BBQ
desc: Southern BBQ in a historic brick building on Main Street, known for hand-pulled pork, ribs and beef burnt ends.

name: The Butcher and Bottle
desc: Chef-driven steakhouse with Southern roots on Roswell Street in downtown Alpharetta, part of a small north Georgia restaurant group that also runs other Butcher & Bottle locations. It focuses on upscale steaks and Southern plates with handcrafted drinks, in a walkable spot near City Center.
tips: It operates as an evening dinner spot, so plan on a dinner visit rather than lunch.
Downtown parking fills on weekends; the City Center decks are a short walk away.

name: The Southern Porch
desc: Fried green tomatoes, pimento cheese and biscuits and gravy served on a breezy screened-in porch downtown.

name: Citizen Soul
desc: California cuisine with a Southern accent in the heart of downtown.

name: Hen Mother Cookhouse
desc: Homemade comfort food and baked goods downtown; a staple for breakfast and brunch.

name: Up On The Roof
desc: Rooftop brunch above downtown with mimosa carafes, bayou crab cakes and challah French toast.

name: Maple Street Biscuit Company
desc: Flaky biscuit sandwiches with inventive fillings, served downtown.

name: Crust Pasta & Pizzeria
desc: Tuscan-style antipasti, pasta and pizza on South Main Street.
address: 131 S Main St, Ste H, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: Fogon and Lions
desc: Spanish, Latin American and Caribbean-inspired plates and drinks just off the Town Green.
hours: Tue-Thu 4-9pm; Fri 4-10pm; Sat 11am-10pm; Sun 11am-9pm; Mon closed

name: Butcher and Brew
desc: Scratch-made food paired with a rotating lineup of local Georgia beers at Alpharetta City Center.

name: Cabernet Steakhouse
desc: Club-like steakhouse and seafood room on Windward Parkway with a deep wine list; an Alpharetta institution.

name: Pampas Steakhouse
desc: Argentinian-style steakhouse cooking over wood embers on a custom grill.
address: 10970-A State Bridge Rd, Johns Creek, GA 30022

name: Vinny's on Windward
desc: Longtime Windward Italian known for risotto, gnocchi and tiramisu.
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; Dinner Mon-Thu & Sun 4-9pm, Fri-Sat 4-10pm

name: Ippolito's Family Style Italian
desc: Local Italian restaurant group serving north metro Atlanta since 1989, with a casual, friendly dining room on Highway 9 at Windward. The menu covers homemade sandwiches, pizzas, calzones and pastas, plus chicken, veal and seafood specialties, a broad wine list and desserts.
tips: Carry-out is available if you want a family pasta night at home.
Open every day from 11am, so it works for an early weekday lunch.

name: Nahm Fine Thai Cuisine
desc: Upscale Thai on Windward Parkway, run by chef Nahm Thongyoung since 2006.
address: 5310 Windward Pkwy, Ste C, Alpharetta, GA 30004
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-2:30pm; Dinner Mon-Thu 5-9:30pm, Fri-Sat 5-10pm, Sun 2-9pm

name: Secreto Southern Kitchen & Bar
desc: Farm-to-table Southern dishes on Windward Parkway.

name: Tarahumata Mexican Grill & Tequila Bar
desc: Tarahumata Mexican Grill & Tequila Bar has served Windward Parkway since 2006, pairing Mexican and Tex-Mex plates with tapas-style small plates and a list of more than 150 tequilas. Popular picks include grilled hanger steak, calamari, tostadas, mini burgers and prawns, with seating inside or on the patio.
tips: Ask the bar for a tequila flight to sample from the 150-plus bottle list.
The outdoor patio is a good pick on mild evenings.

name: Curry Pizza House
desc: Curry Pizza House, paired here with Hidden Tap & Barrel, tops craft pizzas with Indian curries and spices, from tandoori chicken to paneer, alongside wings and a full bar. The Windward Parkway space has indoor and outdoor seating, and the menu includes several vegan pizzas made with gluten-free crust and vegan cheese.
address: 5530 Windward Pkwy, Ste C-300, Alpharetta, GA 30004
tips: Service can slow down at peak dinner hours, so order ahead for pickup on busy nights.
Ask about the vegan pizzas with gluten-free crust if anyone in your group has dietary limits.

name: The Original Pancake House
desc: The pancake specialist, serving its famous apple pancake and Dutch baby on Windward Parkway.

name: J Christopher's
desc: Breakfast, brunch and lunch standby at Windward Plaza.

name: Luci's Ristorante Italiano
desc: Windward Italian steakhouse serving 35-day dry-aged cuts alongside classic pastas.

name: Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant
desc: Casual dining paired with a Napa-style tasting room pouring its own award-winning wines, on North Point Parkway.

name: Food Terminal
desc: Malaysian street-food favorite in the North Point corridor, from the team behind the Atlanta original.

name: Mama's Pizza
desc: Long-running North Point pizzeria known for New York-style pies and slices, plus Sicilian squares, stromboli, calzones, meatball subs and fresh salads. It has been at its North Point Parkway location since 2013 and is a regular pick among Alpharetta locals for a quick slice or a family pizza night.
tips: Regulars recommend the Sicilian pie paired with a Greek salad.
Try fried pepperoni as a topping, which reviewers compare to bacon.

name: Chronic Tacos
desc: California-style tacos, burritos and quesadillas near North Point.
address: 970 North Point Dr, Suite B160, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen
desc: Gulf Coast and Cajun seafood with a famous Sunday brunch, just off GA 400.

name: Marlow's Tavern
desc: Neighborhood tavern known for its prime rib French dip, fish tacos and burgers.

name: Village Tavern
desc: Polished American tavern on Rainwater Drive with a big patio.
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3pm; Dinner Sun-Mon 3-9pm, Tue-Thu 3-10pm, Fri-Sat 3-11pm

name: Firebirds Wood Fired Grill
desc: American grill known for wood-fired steaks and seafood.

name: Pure Taqueria
desc: Stylish Mexican spot known for seafood dishes and strong margaritas.

name: Delbar
desc: Middle Eastern favorite on Old Milton known for hummus, labneh, falafel and chicken kofta.
hours: Dinner Tue-Thu 5-9pm, Fri-Sat 4-10pm, Sun 4-9pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3:45pm

name: Jerusalem Bakery & Grill
desc: Family-owned Middle Eastern bakery, grill and pizzeria on Old Milton Parkway, open since 2009, with shawarma, kebabs, hot sandwiches and breads baked in-house. A small market inside stocks spices, olives, rice, teas, tahini, cooking oils and cheeses for cooking at home.
address: 4150 Old Milton Pkwy, Ste 129, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Pick up fresh bread and pantry items from the in-store market after your meal.
It opens at 9am daily, so it works for an early bakery run.

name: Efendi Mediterranean Restaurant
desc: Turkish Mediterranean restaurant that opened as Cafe Efendi in 2004 and rebranded as Efendi Mediterranean in 2026. The menu runs from hummus, falafel, kebabs and grilled seafood to lahmacun, Iskender and Turkish breakfast, and the space includes a cocktail bar, hookah lounge and enclosed patio.
tips: A gyro lunch is served until 4pm every day.
Evenings can bring live music and belly dancing; call ahead if you want a quieter dinner.

name: Kailash Parbat
desc: North Indian and Sindhi cuisine on North Main Street.

name: Sushi Sumo
desc: Neighborhood sushi and pan-Asian spot at Old Alabama Square.
address: 3005 Old Alabama Rd, Ste 440, Alpharetta, GA 30022
hours: Mon & Wed-Fri 11am-11pm; Sat 12-11pm; Sun 3:30-11pm; Tue closed

name: True Food Kitchen
desc: Health-driven menu of bowls, salads and lean proteins.

name: Valor Coffee
desc: Downtown Alpharetta's hometown roaster, with indoor and outdoor seating a block off Main Street.

name: Warm Waves Coffee
desc: Cozy downtown coffee shop with comfortable seating and a short food menu.

name: Brewable
desc: Nonprofit coffee cafe in the lobby of the Alpharetta Community Center that provides paid jobs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It serves hot and iced coffee drinks with quiche, scones and cake pops, and sells T-shirts and artwork, with a dog tie-up area outside.
tips: Grab a coffee before or after an activity at the Alpharetta Community Center.
Try the cake pops, made with cake donated by Cafe Intermezzo.

name: Boarding Pass Coffee
desc: Airline-themed coffee shop complete with real Delta seating.

name: Fuel Coffee
desc: Industrial-style cafe on North Main with breakfast and lunch.
address: 800 N Main St Ste 110, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: The Nest Cafe
desc: Lollipop waffles, croissants and beignets in downtown Alpharetta.

name: Shibam Coffee
desc: Handcrafted drinks and light bites in the North Point corridor.
address: 4000 North Point Pkwy Ste 900, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: Argentis Bakery
desc: Downtown bakery where everything is gluten- and dairy-free.
address: 42 Milton Ave Ste B, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: Dolce Spoon
desc: Handmade desserts and gelato downtown.

name: Vincent Bakery
desc: Korean bakery near North Point with pastries, boba and espresso.
address: 5950 North Point Pkwy Ste 129, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: BB's Bagels
desc: Legendary bagels from a tin trailer on McFarland Parkway; go early, they often sell out.

name: Currahee Brewing Company
desc: Downtown taproom pouring Belgian golden ales, German lagers and coffee stouts; outside food welcome.

name: Avalon
desc: Alpharetta's 86-acre upscale mixed-use district: dozens of shops and restaurants along the Boulevard, the Regal Avalon 12 theater, The Hotel at Avalon, and a plaza with bocce, swings and fire pits. Home to a seasonal ice rink, tree lighting and Santa visits each winter.
tips: The seasonal Avalon on Ice rink runs from late November to about mid-January
Parking decks are free; the front rows fill fast on weekends
The Alpha Loop trail connects Avalon to downtown in about a mile

name: Downtown Alpharetta
desc: Alpharetta's walkable heart: 50+ shops and restaurants around Main Street, the Town Green with its splash fountain, City Hall, a self-guided arts walk of nearly 20 sculptures, and the Saturday farmers market in season.
tips: The Saturday farmers market runs April through November on the Town Green
Street parking fills on weekends; the City Center deck is the move
Nearly 20 sculptures line the self-guided arts walking tour

name: Big Creek Greenway
desc: Alpharetta's signature trail: about 9 miles of wide paved path along Big Creek for walking, biking and skating, plus mountain-bike trails and a wetland boardwalk spur. Free, dawn to dusk, with access points at Rock Mill, Haynes Bridge, Northpoint and more.
tips: Popular access points: Rock Mill Park, Haynes Bridge Park and Northpoint Parkway
Mornings and weekdays are quietest; weekends get busy with bikes
The boardwalk sections flood occasionally after heavy rain

name: Ameris Bank Amphitheatre
desc: Alpharetta's 12,000-seat outdoor concert venue in a wooded setting at Encore Park, hosting major country, rock and pop tours from spring through fall.
tips: The lawn is first-come; bring a blanket (chairs are usually rentable)
Traffic stacks up on Westside Parkway before shows, so arrive early
The season generally runs April through October

name: Wills Park
desc: Alpharetta's largest park at about 110 acres: sports fields, three playgrounds, a pool, disc golf, a community garden, loop trails and the Wills Park Equestrian Center.

name: Webb Bridge Park
desc: 109-acre park with sports fields, a lake, an arboretum and a crushed-limestone trail that loops about 1.7 miles along a creek.

name: North Park
desc: 97-acre park with sports fields, a lake, a reflection garden, a 1-mile paved trail and the city's Adult Activity Center.

name: Brooke Street Park
desc: 5-acre passive park behind City Hall with an arboretum, paved trail, stream, sculptures and a covered bandstand.

name: Rock Mill Park
desc: 20-acre park on Kimball Bridge Road with pavilions, an environmental education area and a popular Big Creek Greenway trailhead.

name: Union Hill Park
desc: City of Alpharetta park on 13 acres reached from Union Hill Road off Windward Parkway. It has an outdoor pop-up skate park, a covered roller hockey rink, a pavilion and concession stand available to rent, on-site parking and an access point for the Big Creek Greenway trail.
tips: Use the park as a parking and starting point for a Big Creek Greenway walk or ride.
Book the pavilion through the city ahead of time for parties or group events.

name: Cogburn Road Park
desc: Nearly 6-acre neighborhood park with an arboretum, pavilions and a Play Me Again piano.

name: Waggy World Paw Park
desc: 1.5-acre fenced, off-leash dog park for well-behaved pups.

name: Alpha Loop
desc: A paved urban trail linking Downtown Alpharetta and Avalon, about a mile each way, with public art and pocket parks along the route.

name: Alpharetta Farm at Old Rucker Park
desc: A 2-acre working farm with gardens, a greenhouse and an outdoor classroom.

name: Silos Park
desc: Small one-acre park in the Crabapple area built around four historic grain silos. Historical photos and a display explain how the silos once stored grain for local farms, making it a quick stop for a bit of local history while visiting Crabapple's shops and restaurants.
tips: Plan it as a short stop rather than a destination; the park is just one acre.
Pair it with a stroll through nearby Crabapple shops and restaurants.

name: Topgolf Alpharetta
desc: Point-scoring golf games for every skill level, with food and drinks served to your climate-controlled bay. Open year-round.

name: Main Event Entertainment
desc: Bowling, laser tag, high ropes, billiards and a huge game room under one roof.

name: Fairway Social
desc: Sports simulators, a nine-hole synthetic-turf putting course, food, drinks and live music.

name: Roaring Social
desc: Speakeasy-style lounge with boutique bowling, live music, cocktails and dinner.

name: Adventure Air Sports
desc: Trampoline and family entertainment center with racing slides and virtual reality.

name: Immersive Gamebox
desc: Private interactive game rooms with projection mapping and motion tracking; 60-minute sessions for groups.

name: Odyssey Escape Game
desc: Team escape rooms with hidden clues and puzzles.

name: Urban Escape Games
desc: Locally designed escape rooms near North Point where teams have one hour to find clues, crack codes and solve puzzles to get out of a themed room. It bills itself as the first escape game company in Georgia and is popular for family outings, date nights and corporate team building, with debriefs offered for company groups.
address: 20 Mansell Ct E, Ste 275, Alpharetta, GA 30076
tips: Book online in advance; games run on scheduled time slots.
Corporate groups can ask for a personalized debrief after the game.

name: The Velvet Note
desc: An intimate acoustic jazz listening room, open Thursday through Sunday, with national acts and a 1924 Baldwin baby grand.

name: Matilda's Under the Pines
desc: Bring-a-picnic outdoor music venue with live shows in spring and summer.

name: Wills Park Equestrian Center
desc: A 50-acre equestrian facility inside Wills Park with a covered arena and four outdoor rings, hosting horse shows, rodeos and dog shows year-round.

name: RiverPines Golf
desc: Public 27-hole golf facility, including a separate par-3 course, on the Johns Creek border.
address: 4775 Old Alabama Rd, Johns Creek, GA 30022

name: Alpharetta Farmers Market
desc: Saturday-morning market on the Town Green, April through November, with local growers, bakers, makers and flowers.

name: Alpharetta Food Truck Alley
desc: Ten or more food trucks and live music on Old Roswell Street, the fourth Thursday of each month from April through October. Bring a chair.

name: Alpharetta and Old Milton County History Museum
desc: Free museum inside City Hall telling Alpharetta's story from Cherokee territory through its years as the Milton County seat to today's tech economy.

name: Alpharetta Arts Center
desc: 10,000-square-foot center on Canton Street with a black-box theater, visual arts and clay studios and rotating gallery exhibits.

name: Mansell House and Gardens
desc: A 1912 Queen Anne home and gardens, home of the Alpharetta & Old Milton County Historical Society; tours by appointment and a popular wedding venue.
hours: Mon 11am-2pm; Wed & Fri 10am-2pm; tours by appointment

name: Downtown Alpharetta History Walk
desc: Free self-guided walking tour with more than 20 historic markers spread through downtown Alpharetta, all within easy walking distance. The markers cover the industries that once drove the local economy and buildings that served very different purposes in the past. It suits all ages and is open year-round.
address: 178 S Main St, Ste 200, Alpharetta, GA 30009
tips: Pick up the free History Walk brochure at the Alpharetta Welcome Center (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm, Sat 10am-4pm).
The free City Tours app maps each landmark if you would rather skip the paper brochure.

name: Walk of Memories
desc: Veterans memorial at American Legion Post 201 with nearly 8,000 engraved bricks honoring Georgians who served in every branch. Monuments mark World War II, Korea and Vietnam, and displays include a Cold War-era M60 tank, a UH-1 Huey flown in the 1968 Tet Offensive, a Navy twin 40mm gun and an Air Force T-33 trainer.
tips: Engraved bricks can be added for a $50 donation through the Post.
Download the Walk of Memories brochure before you go to learn the story behind each display.

name: North Point Mall
desc: Alpharetta's regional mall, anchored by Dillard's, JCPenney, Macy's and Von Maur. The city approved a major mixed-use redevelopment of the site in 2026, so expect changes in the years ahead.

name: All Inspired Boutiques
desc: Downtown Alpharetta boutique on Canton Street with hand-picked women's clothing, accessories, home decor and gifts. Alongside current fashion it showcases Georgia-made art, jewelry and pottery, which makes it a good stop for a locally made present while walking the downtown shopping district.
tips: Look for the Georgia-made jewelry and pottery when shopping for a local gift.
Combine a visit with other shops and restaurants along Canton Street.

name: Sis + Moons
desc: Eclectic downtown shop on Milton Avenue mixing home goods, local art and vintage finds with candles and clothing. In back, The Treehouse at Sis and Moon's operates as a working studio and art gallery that hosts art classes, so the shop doubles as a creative hub in the downtown district.
tips: Ask about upcoming classes at The Treehouse studio in the back.
Its sister shop Korner Soak, for bath goods and loungewear, is a few doors away on Milton Avenue.

name: Korner Soak
desc: Small downtown Alpharetta shop specializing in bath and beauty products along with pajamas and loungewear. It comes from the sisters behind Sis + Moons and sits on the same stretch of Milton Avenue, making it an easy stop for cozy gifts, self-care items and soft layers while browsing downtown.
tips: Pop over to Sis + Moons on the same block for art and vintage finds.
A good stop for ready-made gifts like bath sets and loungewear.

name: Clothes Horse
desc: Menswear shop on Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta that bills itself as having north Atlanta's best collection of men's business casual apparel. Expect upscale casual shirts, trousers and layers for the office or weekends, with personal service from a small independent store.
tips: A good place to build out a business casual wardrobe in one stop.
Park once downtown and walk to Milton Avenue's other boutiques nearby.

name: The Red Hound
desc: Gift and home decor shop at Alpharetta City Center that moved from its original Johns Creek location. It carries gifts for babies, kids, teachers, graduates, brides and hostesses, mixing one-of-a-kind pieces from local and regional artists with accessories and national brands.
tips: Handy for last-minute baby, hostess or teacher gifts.
Look for pieces by local and regional artists that are hard to find elsewhere.

name: Comeback Vinyl
desc: Downtown vinyl shop with new and used records and a listening station.

name: Alpharetta Outfitters
desc: Downtown outdoor shop focused on fly fishing, with rods, reels, flies and gear alongside hiking and camping equipment and outdoor supplies. It also offers fly-fishing classes and guided trips, so it is a useful first stop for beginners and for anglers planning a north Georgia trout outing.
tips: Ask about beginner fly-fishing classes before buying a full setup.
Call ahead to set up a guided trip.

name: The Ginger Room
desc: Tea room in one of downtown Alpharetta's oldest buildings, serving traditional British high tea by reservation along with local and international loose-leaf teas. It is also known for all-natural ginger juices, including signature Ginger Yums in 17 flavors that can be mixed into more than 100 combinations.
tips: Reserve ahead for high tea, especially on weekends.
Take-home and gift tins of tea make easy presents.

name: Queen of Hearts
desc: Large antique and home furnishings market on North Main Street, part of a group with Alpharetta, Buford and Marietta locations and more than 550 dealers in all. Booths carry vintage and antique furniture, lighting, decor, collectibles and sports memorabilia, plus DIY furniture paints and monthly workshops.
tips: Allow plenty of time; the booths take a while to browse.
Check the monthly workshop schedule for furniture painting classes.

name: Designer Consigner
desc: Consignment boutique on North Main Street selling gently used designer and high-end women's clothing, shoes and accessories. Casual labels are sorted on racks by size, style and color, while higher-end designer pieces hang on wall displays that rotate with current trends.
tips: Check the wall racks for the higher-end designer pieces.
Call ahead to confirm hours and consignment drop-off policies.

name: Urban Hardware
desc: Large independent hardware, home and garden store on Haynes Bridge Road affiliated with True Value. Beyond tools, paint and repair supplies, it carries patio furniture, home and garden goods and seasonal holiday decor, with the hands-on service of a local store and a big-box sized selection.
tips: Check here for patio furniture and seasonal decor, not just hardware.
Staff can help track down odd parts for home repairs.

name: Neese Heating, AC & Plumbing
desc: Locally owned since 1992, handling HVAC and plumbing with 24/7 emergency service.

name: Climate Heroes Air Conditioning
desc: Family-owned AC repair, installation and furnace service on Hembree Road.

name: 4 Seasons Heating & Air
desc: Veteran HVAC company offering installation, repair and duct cleaning.

name: Gagne Heating & Air Conditioning
desc: Residential and commercial HVAC with a Comfort Club maintenance membership.

name: Superior Indoor Comfort
desc: Residential and commercial HVAC and indoor air quality specialists.

name: Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Alpharetta
desc: Locally owned 24/7 plumbing franchise serving Alpharetta and North Fulton.
address: 1360 Union Hill Rd, Suite 3H, Alpharetta, GA 30004

name: Good Ol'Boys Plumbing
desc: Water heaters, drains and sewer lines with same-day service.

name: Zippy Plumber
desc: Underground plumbing, sewer lines and camera inspections.

name: Hall Family Dental Care
desc: General and cosmetic dentistry led by Dr. Chase Hall, with an in-house savings plan for uninsured patients.
address: 3400 Old Milton Pkwy, Bldg A, Suite 540, Alpharetta, GA 30005

name: Smile Makers of Georgia
desc: Full-service family dental practice with Saturday hours, serving Alpharetta and Milton.
address: 3275 North Point Pkwy, Suite 103, Alpharetta, GA 30005

name: Old Milton Dental
desc: Three-dentist practice offering preventive, restorative and cosmetic care, including implants and TMJ treatment.
address: 4165 Old Milton Pkwy, Suite 270, Alpharetta, GA 30005

name: Windward Dental Care
desc: General and cosmetic dentistry, including implants and whitening, on the Highway 9 corridor.

name: Stone Dental Associates
desc: General, cosmetic, orthodontic and oral surgery services under one roof.
address: 4205 North Point Pkwy, Bldg E, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: All On Smile Georgia
desc: Implant and cosmetic dentistry center with an oral surgeon and cosmetic dentist on staff.

name: Advanced Cosmetic and Family Dentistry
desc: Preventive, cosmetic and restorative family dental care.
address: 4205 North Point Pkwy, Bldg D, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: RA Dental Studio
desc: Family-friendly preventive, cosmetic and restorative dentistry.

name: Alpharetta Smile Center
desc: General, cosmetic and restorative dentistry in Alpharetta.

name: Veterinary Medical Center
desc: Full-service animal hospital founded in 1982, with emergency care, boarding and extended hours.

name: easyvet Alpharetta
desc: Doctor-owned cat and dog clinic using Fear Free handling, with walk-in sick visits.

name: Midway Animal Hospital
desc: AAHA-accredited since 1988, offering dental, ultrasound and grooming.

name: Webb Bridge Animal Hospital
desc: Surgery, dental and after-hours emergency services.
hours: Mon & Wed 8am-6pm; Tue, Thu, Fri 8:30am-5pm; Sat 8:30am-4pm; Sun closed

name: Mill Creek Animal Hospital
desc: Wellness, surgery and dentistry; caring for Alpharetta pets since 1996.

name: Lotus Animal Hospital
desc: Family-owned practice offering surgery, acupuncture, senior pet care and weekend hours.
hours: Mon, Thu, Fri 7:30am-5pm; Wed 7:30am-12pm; Sat 7:30am-4pm; Sun 9am-4pm; Tue closed
address: 5215 Windward Pkwy, Suite B-2, Alpharetta, GA 30004

name: Milton Animal Hospital
desc: Owner-operated hospital known for TPLO knee surgery and senior pet care, serving Alpharetta, Milton and Roswell.

name: Veterinary Specialists of Greater Atlanta
desc: Specialty and 24/7 emergency hospital with surgery, oncology and critical care.

name: VEG ER for Pets
desc: 24/7 emergency clinic for dogs, cats and exotics.

name: German Car Repair
desc: German Car Repair, Inc. is an independent service and repair shop on Atlanta Highway that works only on Porsche, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volkswagen and MINI. Beyond routine service it handles performance and suspension upgrades, race prep, tech inspections, and interior and convertible top repair.
tips: Repairs carry a 12-month or 12,000-mile warranty
Offers Noelle Performance software upgrades for some BMW, Porsche and Mercedes models

name: Eurofed Automotive
desc: Eurofed Automotive's Alpharetta shop on Old Roswell Road services European makes such as BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volkswagen, Porsche, Volvo and MINI. It is one of about two dozen Eurofed locations and offers diagnostics, factory-interval maintenance and repairs with digital inspections that show you what the car needs.
address: 11090 Old Roswell Rd, Ste B, Alpharetta, GA 30009
tips: Closed on weekends, so plan drop-offs for weekdays
Digital vehicle inspections let you review findings before approving work

name: Japanese Automotive Professional Service
desc: Japanese Automotive has repaired Asian vehicles in the Atlanta area since 1989, with ASE-certified technicians who focus on Honda, Toyota, Nissan, Subaru and other Japanese brands. The Maxwell Road shop handles routine maintenance through complex diagnostics and has a second location in Cumming.
tips: Loaner cars are available at the Alpharetta location
Qualifying repairs carry a 3-year/36,000-mile warranty

name: 4A Auto A/C & Repair
desc: 4A Auto A/C & Repair is a USMC veteran-owned, father-and-son mobile mechanic service run by Chris and Alex that serves Alpharetta, Johns Creek and nearby cities. They come to your home or workplace for car A/C diagnosis and repair, battery and starting problems, warning lights and used-car inspections.
tips: Posted prices include A/C diagnosis from $195 and used-car inspections from $245
Call or text during service hours; closed Sundays

name: BG Auto Care

Inquiries are usually answered within 24 hours on business days

Second location at 1505 Northside Blvd in Cumming

Newborns should be seen within 48 hours of hospital discharge; call to schedule

address: 3180 North Point Pkwy, Suite 410, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Closed on weekends, so plan sick visits for weekdays
Hours can vary; call ahead to confirm

address: 11525 Haynes Bridge Rd, Suite 200, Alpharetta, GA 30009
tips: Saturday morning sick appointments are offered at this office only
Phone lines are open weekdays 8:30am-4:30pm

tips: Membership model with no insurance billing; ask about costs
Call 770-475-9924 or use the site form to book a consult

tips: Initial consultations are free
Ask about the 7 and Up check-up for younger kids

Appointments are by schedule; online booking is available

hours: Mon, Tue, Thu 8am-4pm; Wed and Fri closed
tips: Accepting new patients; book online
Closed Wednesdays and Fridays

name: Atlanta Center for Dermatologic Disease
desc: Dermatology group with an Alpharetta office in Building C of the 3400 Old Milton Parkway medical campus, plus offices elsewhere in metro Atlanta including Roswell, Cumming and Sandy Springs. It provides medical dermatology for skin, hair and nail conditions along with skin checks for adults and children.
address: 3400 Old Milton Pkwy, Building C, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Office is in Building C of the 3400 Old Milton Pkwy campus
Call to confirm hours and which providers see patients in Alpharetta

name: Windward Eye Care
desc: Locally owned optometry office opened in 2003 by Drs. Thomas Arey, Sean Alexander and Michael Walker, operating with sister office Alpharetta Eye Clinic under Atlanta Eye Care. It offers adult and children's eye exams, contact lenses, eyeglasses and sunglasses, plus LASIK and cataract consultations.
address: 5315 Windward Pkwy, Suite F, Alpharetta, GA 30004
tips: Saturday hours are offered at this Windward office only
Request appointments through the online form

name: Eye Associates of North Atlanta
desc: Private ophthalmology practice of board-certified ophthalmologist and cataract surgeon Dr. Anand K. Shah, located near North Point Mall between GA-400 exits 9 and 10. Services include eye exams, cataract surgery, glaucoma, diabetic eye exams, dry eye and macular degeneration care.
address: 5755 North Point Pkwy, Suite 94, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Request appointments online; general line is 470-767-8287
Accepts most major medical insurance plans

Board-certified ENT physicians and audiologists see adults and children for sinus and nasal issues, allergies, sleep and snoring, voice and swallowing, and hearing.
address: 3333 Old Milton Pkwy, Suite 520, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Same-week appointments are often available
Audiology services are offered at this location

address: 3330 Preston Ridge Rd, Suite 240, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Office is in Suite 240 at 3330 Preston Ridge Rd
Check Northside's provider pages to choose a doctor before booking

name: Pediatric ENT of Atlanta
desc: Pediatric ear, nose and throat practice in Suite 275 at 3300 Old Milton Parkway, focused on infants, children and teens. Physicians listed for this office include pediatric otolaryngologists Dr. Erik Bauer and Dr. Megan Ballard and otolaryngologist Dr. Paula Harmon.
address: 3300 Old Milton Pkwy, Suite 275, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Office is in Suite 275 at 3300 Old Milton Pkwy
Many visits start with a pediatrician referral; ask your insurer

name: Northside Orthopedics - Sports Medicine

Its team covers hip, knee and shoulder surgery as well as non-operative orthopedics and pediatric sports medicine, with physicians Dr. Jon Erik Minter, Dr. Christopher Potts and Dr. Joseph Powers.
address: 3400 Old Milton Pkwy, Building C, Suite 190, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Office is in Building C, Suite 190
Closes early on Fridays at 2:30pm

hours: Mon and Wed 7am-4pm, Tue and Thu 8am-6pm, Fri 7am-1pm
tips: Now branded Benchmark Physical Therapy; search that name in maps
Located in the Aldi center across from Target on Hwy 9

name: North Fulton Physical Therapy
desc: Independent outpatient physical therapy and sports medicine clinic in Suite 126 at Founders Park, off Founders Parkway. It provides orthopedic, sports and post-surgical rehabilitation using manual therapy and therapeutic exercise for active adults and athletes.
tips: Direct access is available, so a physician referral may not be needed
Call to confirm hours and insurance before your first visit

name: North Atlanta Spine
desc: Chiropractic office in Suite 96 at 5755 North Point Parkway offering spinal adjustments, spinal decompression and massage therapy. It works with patients dealing with neck and back problems as well as people seeking ongoing chiropractic care.
address: 5755 North Point Pkwy, Suite 96, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Hours vary by day, with afternoon-only sessions on Tuesday and Thursday
Book online through the website

desc: Northpoint Family Chiropractic Center, a family chiropractic practice led by Dr. Colin in Suite 101 at 3180 North Point Parkway. It sees patients of all ages, from infants to grandparents, and offers gentle chiropractic adjustments for the whole family.
address: 3180 North Point Pkwy, Suite 101, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Tuesday and Thursday hours are at a separate home office; confirm location
Saturday hours run only 10am to noon

name: Chiropractic Health Clinics
desc: Chiropractic practice, also known as Atlanta Chiropractic Group, run by Dr. Alex Mahyar in Suite 750 on Holcomb Bridge Road. It uses the Activator, Diversified and Thompson techniques plus massage, cupping, disc decompression and laser therapy, and handles auto accident injury care.
address: 2650 Holcomb Bridge Rd, Suite 750, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Treats auto accident injuries as part of personal injury cases
Call 678-381-1184 to set up a consultation

name: Inner Compass Counseling
desc: Group counseling practice with an Alpharetta office in Suite 227 at 5755 North Point Parkway, plus offices in Cumming and Marietta. Therapists see kids ages 5 to 12, teens, young adults, individuals, couples and families, with approaches that include EMDR and DBT.
address: 5755 North Point Pkwy, Suite 227, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Virtual counseling is offered as well as in-person sessions
Request an appointment through the website form

address: 5755 North Point Pkwy, Suite 280, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Evening and weekend appointments are offered
Schedule a call through the website to be matched with a counselor

tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
The Eagle Update newsletter on the school site covers news and events

name: Cambridge High School

tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
New families start with the New Enrollments page on the school site

tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Middle school day runs 8:55am to 4:05pm

name: Holcomb Bridge Middle School
desc: Fulton County Schools public middle school for grades 6-8 on Holcomb Bridge Road near the Alpharetta and Roswell line. Students have access to counseling, talented and gifted services, school clubs, athletics and fine arts programs.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Middle school day runs 8:55am to 4:05pm

name: Hopewell Middle School
desc: Fulton County Schools public middle school for grades 6-8 on Cogburn Road in Milton, serving north Alpharetta and Milton addresses. The school has a bilingual community liaison for families along with counseling, clinic services, clubs and athletics.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Ask the front office about the bilingual community liaison if needed

name: Alpharetta Elementary School
desc: Fulton County Schools public elementary school, home of the Eagles, on Mayfield Road near downtown Alpharetta. It serves pre-kindergarten through grade 5 and offers special education, talented and gifted (TAG) and ESOL services.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Pre-K seats are filled through the FCS Pre-K lottery

name: Creek View Elementary
desc: Fulton County Schools public elementary school on Webb Bridge Road in the southeast part of Alpharetta, serving kindergarten through grade 5. It follows the district's early elementary bell schedule and offers clinic, counseling and family resources.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Elementary day runs 7:40am to 2:20pm

name: Lake Windward Elementary
desc: Fulton County Schools public elementary school on East Fox Court in the Windward area, serving kindergarten through grade 5. The school site has a welcome section for new families with registration information and back-to-school FAQs.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
See the Welcome New Families page for registration steps

name: New Prospect Elementary
desc: Fulton County Schools public elementary school on Kimball Bridge Road in east Alpharetta. It serves pre-kindergarten through grade 5, with Pre-K seats assigned through the district's annual Pre-K lottery, which opens each winter.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Watch for the FCS Pre-K lottery, which opens in late January

name: Manning Oaks Elementary
desc: Fulton County Schools public elementary school on Cumming Street, just north of downtown Alpharetta, serving kindergarten through grade 5. It follows the district's early elementary bell schedule and offers clinic, counseling and family resources.
tips: Check your address on the FCS attendance zone maps before enrolling
Elementary day runs 7:40am to 2:20pm

desc: Private Christian school and a ministry of First City Church, located on Academy Street in downtown Alpharetta. It serves children from age 2 through 5th grade, with a preschool program and an elementary curriculum that includes Bible, phonics and cursive starting in first grade.
tips: Schedule a tour through the website before applying
Office is reached by following the hallway to the right inside

desc: Christian college-prep school, K-12, on Bethany Bend.

desc: Private school on Cogburn Road, best known for its high school.

name: McGinnis Woods Country Day School
desc: Private school on Faircroft Drive that has served Alpharetta families since 1999, from infant and toddler care through private Pre-K and grades K-8. It is NAEYC, Cognia and Georgia Accrediting Commission accredited and offers before and after school programs.
tips: K-4 classes run 8:30am-3pm and grades 5-8 until 3:30pm
Prospective parents can request a tour online

name: Alpharetta International Academy
desc: Nonsectarian Montessori school founded in 1981 on Webb Bridge Road, serving children from 18 months through grade 8. Programs run from pre-primary and primary/kindergarten through elementary and middle school, with Spanish taught daily from kindergarten.
tips: Book a campus tour before applying; admission is rolling
Montessori program continues through middle school

name: Crabapple Montessori School
desc: Montessori school, preschool through grade 6, in Crabapple.

name: The Goddard School - Windward
desc: Franchise preschool on Windward Parkway, part of The Goddard School network, offering early childhood programs through pre-K. Enrichment listed for this school includes STEAM, robotics, a rock wall, Spanish, world cultures, and yoga and mindfulness.
tips: Availability is limited; schedule a tour early
Open weekdays 7am to 6pm for full-day care

name: The Goddard School - Holcomb Bridge
desc: Franchise preschool on Holcomb Bridge Road, listed by Goddard as The Goddard School of Roswell - Holcomb Bridge despite its Alpharetta address. It offers play-based early childhood programs focused on hands-on learning, exploration and social skills.
tips: Listed under the Roswell - Holcomb Bridge name on Goddard's site
Currently enrolling; schedule a tour online

name: Carrington Academy Alpharetta
desc: Carrington Academy's Alpharetta Avalon campus on Webb Bridge Road, part of a small north metro Atlanta preschool group. It offers daycare and preschool from 6 weeks through Pre-K, plus before and after care and summer camp, using a play-based Links to Learning curriculum.
tips: Call or use Request Information to confirm hours and openings
Before and after care plus summer camp are offered

name: Montessori Scholars Academy
desc: Nonsectarian Montessori school founded in 2011 on Morris Road, listed with a Milton address on its own site. It runs infant, toddler and primary programs with an elementary level, small classes averaging about 8 students, and lead guides with Montessori training.
tips: Book a tour through the school website
Summer camp is offered

name: Amasa Mexican Kitchen
desc: Coastal Mexican spot in Alpharetta City Center from Juan Calle, co-creator of Chicheria Mexican Kitchen and Buena Vida Tapas. The whole menu is gluten-free, with house-made organic blue corn tortillas, ceviches, Baja fish tacos and a whole crispy snapper. It opened in August 2026 in the former Jekyll Brewing space and has a rooftop bar.
tips: Park free in the City Center garage across from the library on Park Plaza, a short walk away
Reservations are available, and weekend brunch plus a happy hour are listed on the website

name: Chuan Tasty
desc: Sichuan restaurant on Windward Parkway that pairs fiery Chengdu-style cooking with American Chinese favorites. Regulars point to the Dan Dan noodles, Mongolian beef, salt and pepper prawns, steamed pork buns and grilled skewers, and the drink list includes Taiwanese, Thai and taro milk teas. Dine-in, takeout and delivery are all offered.
tips: Ask the staff to adjust the spice level if numbing Sichuan heat is not your thing
A dine-in special adds a free cold noodle dish when your table spends $35 or more

name: Thai Candle Seafood & Bar
desc: Upscale but relaxed Thai restaurant at Avalon led by a chef from northern Thailand, with a menu built around fresh seafood. The coastal trio of seared grouper, shrimp and scallops in a coconut sauce is a signature, and desserts include Thai tea creme brulee and green tea cheesecake. A full bar pours wine and cocktails.
tips: Business casual is requested at dinner, so skip athletic wear and hats
The bar serves wine and signature cocktails, and there is a sister location at The Forum in Peachtree Corners

name: Five Daughters Bakery Avalon
desc: Avalon outpost of the family-run Franklin, Tennessee bakery owned by Isaac and Stephanie Meek and their five daughters. It is known for the croissant-style 100 Layer Donut in full and mini sizes, alongside yeast-raised donuts with vegan options, paleo donuts made with gluten-free ingredients, pastries and coffee, all made from scratch daily.
tips: Go early on weekends, since the bakery notes it stays open only until items sell out
Look for the paleo and vegan donuts if anyone in your group avoids gluten or dairy

name: Where's The Scoop
type: Ice cream and bubble tea shop
desc: Dessert bar in Alpharetta City Center that freezes customizable small-batch ice cream to order, in both dairy and vegan versions, with seasonal ingredients and fresh fruit. It also makes bubble tea from brewed tea and ground spices, from taro and Thai tea to rose and vegan horchata, with boba, popping pearls and Oreo toppings, plus coffee.
tips: Closed Mondays and opens at 5pm Tuesday through Thursday, so plan an after-dinner visit
Vegan ice cream is available, which makes it an easy stop for mixed groups
address: 26 Old Roswell St, Ste 102, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: Kilwins Alpharetta
type: Chocolate, fudge and ice cream shop
desc: Locally owned Kilwins confectionery on Market Street in Alpharetta City Center. It sells Mackinac Island fudge, super-premium ice cream, caramel corn and brittle made in copper kettles, hand-dipped caramel apples and Dubai chocolate, and guests can watch small-batch chocolates and fudge being made in the shop.
tips: Pair it with the free splash area on the Town Green by City Hall on warm days
There is a second Kilwins at Halcyon in Forsyth County, so check you are heading to Market Street

name: Lava Island Alpharetta
desc: Indoor play park with tall slides, foam pits, trampolines, obstacle courses, climbing areas and a separate toddler zone, plus glow-in-the-dark themed party rooms. There is no age limit and parents can play too. A full kitchen serves food, sweets, milkshakes and specialty coffee. Passes are sold by the hour or for the full day.
tips: Socks are required for everyone, and every adult must sign a waiver, so sign it online before you arrive
The phone line is text only; infants 11 months and under get in free

name: Play Street Museum Alpharetta
desc: Pretend-play museum for ages 1 to 8 built like a miniature city, with a cafe, doctor's office, fire truck and block area, plus an art station, slime lab and a rotating Discovery Rug exhibit. Weekly themes cover notable people, holidays and cultures, and weekend events include pottery, canvas painting and dino digs.
tips: Reserve a 90-minute weekday session online; walk-ins pay at the door only if space allows
Parents must stay and supervise, and food is not allowed in the play area, though drinks are
address: 11770 Haynes Bridge Rd, Ste 701-702, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: The Slime Factory Alpharetta
desc: Hands-on slime lab inside North Point Mall where kids mix two custom slimes with toppings and scents, then try a gooey sensory pool, a slime wall and photo spots before leaving with a Master Slime Maker certificate. Sessions run 30 to 60 minutes, and the 5,000-square-foot space also hosts birthday parties and field trips.
tips: Everyone needs a waiver, and tickets are required for ages 2 and up
Children under 14 must have an adult with them; party bookings are non-refundable
address: 1000 North Point Cir, Ste 1082, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: Camp Bow Wow Alpharetta
desc: Dog daycare, overnight boarding, grooming and enrichment center with indoor and outdoor play yards. Owners can watch their dogs on live webcams and manage bookings in the Camp app. Boarding cabins come with a cot, fleece blanket and nightly treat, and medication and daytime play during a stay are included rather than billed as extras.
tips: New dogs must pass an interview first, and the first day of daycare is free
Early drop-off starts at 6:45am on weekdays, which helps commuters
address: 1755 Grassland Pkwy, Ste E, Alpharetta, GA 30004

name: Wills Park Vet
desc: General practice animal hospital in the Haynes Bridge Road shopping center offering wellness exams, dental care, spay and neuter surgery, in-house lab work, a pharmacy and travel health certificates. It also offers same-day and drop-off appointments, plans tailored to each pet, and free Happy Visits that help nervous pets get used to the clinic.
tips: Book and chat through the Digitail app, but call the clinic directly for emergencies
The clinic is closed on weekends, so check its Emergency Partners list for after-hours care
address: 11770 Haynes Bridge Rd, Ste 703, Alpharetta, GA 30009

name: Pit Stop for Pets
type: Dog groomer and self-serve dog wash
desc: Independent pet shop in Crabapple, open more than 14 years, that combines professional grooming with self-serve dog wash stations and USA-made food and treats. Grooming visits double as coat health checks, with staff reviewing the coat, skin, ears and body and reporting what they find. It sits behind the historic Silos landmark.
tips: Self-wash happy hour is a $15 flat rate for any size dog, Tuesday to Thursday 3pm-5pm, no appointment needed
Closed Mondays

name: Dave & Buster's Alpharetta
desc: Big arcade and sports bar near North Point Mall with 100-plus games, from racing and shooting games to air hockey and basketball, plus newer attractions like high-tech darts, Social Shuffle and The Arena. Large HD screens show games, and the full restaurant and bar serves food, craft beer and cocktails.
tips: Happy hour runs Monday to Thursday 4pm-7pm with drink specials and half-price appetizers
The Arena and some newer games require players to be 18 or older

name: Activate Alpharetta
desc: Active gaming venue where groups of two to five move through themed rooms like Grid, Mega Laser, Climb, Hoops and Strike, playing short 1 to 3 minute challenges across 10 difficulty levels. Electronic wristbands track every score for a global leaderboard. It is physically demanding, with running, jumping and climbing.
tips: Book ahead online; walk-ins are welcome but not guaranteed, and solo players cannot play
Minimum age is 6, kids 6 to 13 need an adult on site, and closed-toe flat shoes are recommended

name: All Fired Up Alpharetta
desc: Paint-your-own pottery studio on Main Street with hundreds of pieces to choose from, including mugs, plates, bowls and kids' items. There is no studio fee: you pay for the piece, and paint, brushes, glazing and firing are included. It also runs clay hand-building, themed workshops, date nights and birthday parties.
tips: Reserve for weekends, holidays and groups of six or more; a $25 deposit applies and comes off your bill
Unfinished pieces go home with you, and returning to finish costs a $6 sitting fee

name: The Scene Art Gallery
desc: Gallery run by the nonprofit Alpha Arts Guild on the second level of North Point Mall, showing and selling work by Georgia artists. It has about 6,000 square feet of exhibit space plus 5,000 square feet for workshops and open studio time, and hosts a monthly Spotlight Show reception with a collaborative Paint Around session.
tips: Spotlight Show receptions run 5:30pm-7:30pm on a Saturday each month and are a good time to meet the artists

name: Spa Sydell Alpharetta
